recap.workouts:
No gym, no barbell, no class. Saturday was one job, and you did the one job.

RF12 — 91:51, 16.68 km, load 96, avg HR 139 / max 150, RPE 4, paired at 100% compliance. Analysed off the full per-second streams. Nothing came through on the phone today, so this is the file's account of the day rather than yours.

Warm-up 5:01 at 5:44/km, HR 115. The 80-minute Zone 2 block: 14.85 km at 5:23/km, average HR 141, max 150. Cool-down 5:00 at 7:20/km. This morning you were given 5:18/km as the target rather than the 5:01 edge — you ran 5:23 for eighty minutes. That is the assignment, hit.

Ten-minute splits through the block, pace then average HR:
5:08 · 132
5:02 · 140
5:10 · 142
5:17 · 142
5:15 · 143
5:29 · 144
5:58 · 143
6:03 · 144

Read the course before you read the fade. This was an out-and-back with the gradient in it: the first forty minutes gave away 78 m of elevation and the last forty took 82 m back, 79 m of that inside the closing twenty. 157 m of climbing in total, between 1866 and 1971 m. The two slowest splits are the two hilliest, in that order.

Heart rate is the honest headline. Zero seconds above 150 in the entire eighty minutes. 71.5 minutes at Zone 2 heart rate, 8.1 at Zone 1, and not one second in Zone X, Zone 3 or Zone 4. Against a run LTHR of 167 — the number RT19 measured — your ceiling for the whole session was 150. The trend across the block was +0.13 bpm per minute, about eleven beats over eighty minutes, and a good share of that is the normal opening ramp.

The Zone X figure, stated plainly because the week has a record on the line. Per-second pace puts 14.3 minutes in the Zone X band, against 50.6 in Zone 2, 11.6 in Zone 1 and 1.9 quicker still. Where they fell matters: 12.3 of those 14.3 minutes came in the downhill-biased first forty minutes, at heart rates of 133 to 144, and the last twenty minutes contain none at all.

Durability, like for like: measured on near-flat ground only, the first half ran 5:09/km at HR 139.5 and the second half 5:31/km at 143.4 — roughly 9% decoupling with the terrain taken out, against 12% on the raw numbers.
recap.takeaways:
1) Endurance verdict: executed, and executed with the right instrument. You were told to run this off the middle of the band and off heart rate, and the file agrees — 5:23/km against a 5:18 target, and a heart rate that never left Zone 1 or Zone 2 across eighty minutes. On the morning with the block's joint-highest sleeping heart rate and Form at −27.3, that is the version of this session that costs the least and banks the most. Confidence high: per-second streams, 100% compliance, structure fully intact. Consequence: proceed, nothing to protect against.

2) The Zone X minutes are real, and they are gravity. 14.3 of them by pace, and I am not rounding that to zero — week 9 had a clean sheet and it now has a mark on it. But Zone X is expensive because of what it does to you, not because of what it reads on a watch, and by that test today cost nothing: 12.3 of the 14.3 minutes came on the downhill half at 133 to 144 bpm, zero seconds of the session went above 150, and the closing twenty minutes have none. This is not the week-8 leak repeating. That one was 196 to 222 W held on purpose on a rest day; this is a hill doing it to you while your effort stayed put.

3) The one thing worth watching: about 9% decoupling on flat ground, 5:09 at 139.5 becoming 5:31 at 143.4. Note the shape — your pace fell away, your heart rate did not run up. At eighty minutes that reads as aerobic durability, not as anything acute, and the context covers most of it: day six of seven, twenty-four hours off a 78-load threshold run, and the deepest fatigue of the block underneath it. Not a flag today. It is the number I want to watch shrink once a deload actually lands.

4) ADAPT: no-op. RF12 EXECUTED at 100% compliance with the structure intact; no CrossFit and no lifting were prescribed today, so there is nothing else to classify and nothing is owed. Six days of week 9 banked, both hard sessions delivered, and the only thing left on the week is easy.

RAn4 — 45:03, 7.27 km, load 37 against a planned 45, RPE 5, paired cleanly to the planned session. The file splits exactly to the prescription: 15:01 warm-up, then 4 × (2:30 hard / 5:00 jog). Nothing missing, nothing added. The 82% compliance figure is intervals.icu scoring against its own preset zones, not a shortfall — every step is there at full length.

Warm-up: 5:56/km, HR 119 avg, max 132. Honest Z1.

The four reps, target band 3:48–4:17/km:
rep 1 — 4:08/km, HR 131 at the gun to 158 by the end
rep 2 — 4:03/km, 120 to 161
rep 3 — 4:08/km, 126 to 162
rep 4 — 4:03/km, 130 to 176

All four inside the band, total spread across the set five seconds per kilometre, and the last rep tied the fastest. That is exactly the shape this session wants: crisp, repeatable, no decay.

The HR story — and this is precisely why interval averages are useless here: rep 2 carries a LOWER average than rep 1 despite being five seconds per km quicker, purely because you started it from 120 instead of 131. Read the peaks instead: 158 · 161 · 162 · 176. The first three climb four beats in total across the set, which is a tightly controlled ladder. Rep 4 jumps 14 beats at exactly rep 2's pace — a slice of that is the 5 m of climbing inside that rep, the rest is you closing the session hard. 176 is the highest heart rate in your file this block, above Thursday's 173, and it sits at the top of the new Z4 band (167–175), so rep 4 is the only rep that reached Zone 4 by heart rate. Reps 1–3 peaked 158–162, i.e. high Z3. On 2.5-minute reps starting from a fully recovered HR that is normal lag, not a soft effort — pace is the sharp target here, and pace was hit every time.

Recoveries: 8:12 · 9:07 · 8:58 · 8:39 per km, HR dropping to 108 · 101 · 113 · 114. You shed 50-plus beats between every rep. On the day the panel called your worst of the block, that is a body still recovering fast.

Method note: analysed off the workout-matched interval table, which maps 1:1 to the prescribed steps (901 s warm-up, then 150 s / 300 s four times). The per-second stream pass wasn't available this evening — the Drive folder didn't mount into the compute sandbox — so pace is per-rep rather than per-second. Nothing above is estimated.
recapPrev.takeaways:
1) The run verdict: clean. Four reps inside the pace band, five seconds per km of spread across the whole set, the last one tied fastest, HR shedding 50+ beats in every recovery, and no drift signal anywhere. Load 37 — a fraction of Thursday. As stimulus maintenance it did exactly its job, and there is no fatigue flag in the trace. Confidence: high on the pace read, medium on the HR read (per-rep peaks rather than per-second plateaus).

2) The call, straight. I recommended cutting RAn4 this morning at readiness 27 and you ran it — second day running that you overrode me and the file came back clean. What I actually think, rather than just conceding: the execution was good, and a load of 37 is not what turns a deload into Week 4 again. But two overrides in two days is a pattern worth naming, and the readiness signal — sleeping HR elevated a fifth straight morning, breathing now flagged too, Form −25.8 — still hasn't been paid for. One well-run session doesn't settle it. Tomorrow is where it gets settled.

3) ADAPT: no-op. RAn4 EXECUTED at full structure, Cutthroat done heavier than called but genuinely easy by HR, hypertrophy exact at the deload dose. Nothing in the remaining week moves — and on a deload nothing gets added, ever.

4) Lateral raise 20 lb × 20 tops the range: banked, not applied, per the deload rule. Week 9 now opens with lat pulldown to 190, face pull to 85, leg curl to 50, overhead triceps ext up one step, and lateral raise up one step. Five bumps waiting, all earned this week without spending them.
